art.title: The Trojans Building the Temple to Venus and Making Offerings at Anchises's Grave in Sicily
art.why: An Aeneid scene (Book V): the Trojans honouring Aeneas's dead father, which is pietas itself. No NGA painting of Aeneas fleeing Troy. The gallery's description is brief (a landscape, people gathering, a building under construction): describe only that.

No NGA open-access painting of Dido and Aeneas. Girodet's Coriolanus Taking Leave of his Family (eedab1c0-c052-4a82-9c63-e03f95d1ca0e, free) shows a Roman leaving his weeping family, but it is a different story; not claimed.

art.title: The Triumph of Camillus
art.why: A Roman triumph: the conqueror enthroned, armed men, the procession to the city gates. Rome's mission to 'war down the proud' as Rome celebrated it.

art.title: Lucretia
art.why: Livy's story of Lucretia (Livy I.57–60) is how Romans told the birth of the republic (509 BC). No NGA senate or Cincinnatus. The lecture must tell the story plainly; the look describes only the woman with the dagger.
No NGA open-access painting of a lawgiver or Justice personified found (searched 'justice', 'scales', 'blindfold', 'lawgiver').

art.title: The Rape of the Sabine Women
art.why: Rome's founding violence, which Augustine himself holds up against Rome's glory (City of God II.17). No NGA Colosseum. Handle the subject soberly.
Wanted the Forum or Justice. The Forum at Pompeii, Panini's Pantheon and Hubert Robert's Ponte Salario are claimed by other journeys. None left that fits.

music.why: The spec's choice: English music on an ancient theme, for a journey about what an old civilisation handed on.
Purcell's Dido and Aeneas would be the piece; it is not in music.json (flag).

flags: Music is very thin: one piece in seven sessions, as the spec allows.

Session 6's painting is a scene of abduction: the drafter should decide whether it is suitable; Rembrandt's Lucretia (session 4) also shows a woman about to kill herself. If the reviewer prefers, swap one for null.
